groups.title: Laravel Validation
groups.question: Your controllers are full of validation rules and permission checks, and you need a rule that a booking date falls on a weekday. Explain how Laravel organises validation.

followUps.Form Request Classes and Authorization: What does a Form Request class hold and why use one?
followUps.Custom Validation Rules: How would you write a custom validation rule?

evidence.text: A Form Request holds the validation rules for one request.
It also has an authorize method for permission checks.
Controllers stay thin and only receive validated data.
A custom Rule class or closure holds domain-specific checks.
It returns a clear error message when the check fails.
Rule classes can be reused and tested across requests.

notEnough: Only saying you can write custom rules.

groups.title: Laravel Authentication
groups.question: Your Vue SPA and a mobile app both need to authenticate with Laravel, and only an order's owner may cancel it. Explain how Sanctum and authorization work.

followUps.Laravel Sanctum for SPA Authentication: How does Sanctum authenticate an SPA differently from a mobile app?
followUps.Gates and Policies for Authorization: When would you use a gate and when a policy?

evidence.text: For a first-party SPA, Sanctum uses cookie-based sessions.
For mobile apps and other clients, it issues API tokens.
Using tokens in the browser when cookies would work adds risk and complexity.
Gates are simple checks for actions not tied to one model.
Policies group the rules for one model, like who can update or delete an order.
Controllers call authorize, which returns 403 when the rule fails.

groups.title: CSRF Protection
groups.question: A malicious site tricks logged-in users into submitting a form to your app, and Stripe webhooks are being rejected with 419 errors. Explain how CSRF protection works and when to exclude routes.

followUps.How Laravel's CSRF Token Works: How does Laravel's CSRF token stop forged requests?
followUps.Excluding Routes from CSRF Verification: Why exclude a webhook route from CSRF, and how do you keep it safe?

evidence.text: Laravel creates a CSRF token for each session.
Every state-changing request must include the token, which is compared with the session.
Another site cannot read the token, so its forged requests fail.

notEnough: Only saying CSRF tokens protect forms.

evidence.text: External services like Stripe cannot send your CSRF token.
Those routes are listed as exceptions to CSRF checks.
They must verify the request another way, such as checking the webhook signature.

notEnough: Only saying you add the route to except.

groups.title: Blade Templating
groups.question: A comment containing a script tag runs in other users' browsers, and your Blade views repeat the same card markup. Explain how Blade escapes output and how components help.

followUps.Blade Directives and XSS Prevention: What is the difference between {{ }} and {!! !!} in Blade?
followUps.Blade Components and Slots: How do Blade components and slots help reuse markup?

evidence.text: {{ }} escapes HTML so user content is shown as text.
{!! !!} outputs raw HTML without escaping.
Using raw output on user content allows cross-site scripting.
A Blade component is a reusable piece of UI with its own props.
Slots let callers pass content into named places.
They render on the server, unlike Vue components.
